title: systemd units that behave
subtitle: Turn a command into a supervised service with dependencies, restart policy, and an install target.
objectives: Describe how systemd reaches a target during boot
Read the three sections of a service unit
Write a oneshot or simple service and load it
Enable a unit so it starts at boot
Diagnose a failed unit with status and journal evidence

ex200.evidence: Explain the boot path from firmware to default target.

versionNotes: RHEL 9 and RHEL 10 both use systemd and the same unit-file sections. RHEL 10 ships a newer systemd, so some newer directives may not exist on RHEL 9; check man systemd.directives on the target.
RHEL 10 continues the cgroup v2 model used by RHEL 9. Resource controls belong in the unit, not in ad-hoc shell limits.

sections.title: Load it, enable it, diagnose it

commands.desc: Show running service units and their descriptions.
Show the effective unit file and drop-ins.

commands.cmd: sudo systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl show fieldbook.service -p UnitFileState
commands.desc: Reload unit files after editing or adding them.
Enable at boot and start immediately.
Show state, PID, recent log lines, and exit code.

Check whether the unit is linked into a target.

lab.title: Write and enable a health reporter
lab.scenario: Create a small oneshot service in /etc/systemd/system, reload the manager, enable it, run it, and inspect the journal. Use /usr/local/bin/fieldbook-report as the executable.

steps.text: Inspect the running service set and the boot target.
steps.verify: You can identify running services and the default target.

steps.text: Create the executable that the service will run.
steps.cmd: printf "#!/bin/bash\necho fieldbook-report \$(date)\n" | sudo tee /usr/local/bin/fieldbook-report && sudo chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/fieldbook-report

steps.text: Create a oneshot unit with a description and install target.
steps.verify: The file contains Unit, Service, and Install sections and uses an absolute ExecStart path.

steps.text: Reload systemd, then enable and start the unit.
steps.cmd: sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable --now fieldbook.service
steps.verify: is-enabled returns enabled and the unit reaches a successful state.

steps.text: Inspect status and journal output for the unit.
steps.verify: Status shows the unit and journal entries are filtered to fieldbook.service.

quiz.q: Which section declares dependencies and ordering?
quiz.why: After, Before, Requires, and Wants belong in [Unit].

quiz.q: What must you run after creating a new unit file in /etc/systemd/system?
quiz.why: systemd must reload its unit definitions before it can see the new file.

options: Enables at boot and starts immediately
quiz.why: --now combines the enable action with an immediate start.
